description: Hand-built eval set for the Regs & Tips RAG chatbot (regs_advisor/, POST /regs/ask). Ground truth is verified against regs_advisor/knowledge_base/*.md only. Questions involving a species + 'Zone <digit>' are phrased to avoid triggering the router's separate live-government-data path (engine/question_parsing.py extract_zone/extract_species) so correctness grading stays tied to the static KB rather than today's live numbers from peche.faune.gouv.qc.ca. See eval/run_eval.py and the baseline report for details.

items.question: Quebec regulations say I can only fish with artificial lures, right? No live bait allowed anywhere?
expected_facts: not considered to be bait fish
items.source_ref: regulations_overview.md:62-85 ('Bait rules' -- live baitfish, e.g. minnows, banned province-wide since 2017-04-01; worms, leeches, insects, frogs are not baitfish and remain permitted)
items.notes: False premise, but in the opposite direction from this item's original version: it is NOT true that only artificial lures are allowed -- worms, leeches, insects, and frogs remain legal live bait. The actual ban covers only live baitfish (e.g. minnows), province-wide since 2017-04-01. This item previously assumed no province-wide ban existed at all and would have rewarded an answer saying live baitfish/minnows are permitted; corrected 2026-10-17 after regulations_overview.md's 'Bait rules' section and pinned_rules.json's bait rule were added from the official quebec.ca source (see eval/results/diagnosis_live_bait.md). match_mode 'any' -- pass if the answer contains any one correction phrase, graded as a heuristic (see report). expected_facts revised same day: the first correction used full phrasings ('worms and leeches are allowed') that a correct-but-differently-worded answer won't contain verbatim -- confirmed live, a correct answer explaining the exemption still FAILed grading. Replaced with short fragments (species names, 'not considered ... bait fish') that recur across differently-worded correct answers; none of these words appear in the question itself, so their presence is still a reliable signal the model pulled in the real exemption rather than just echoing the premise.
